summary: King William County, VA tower built 1935 as an 80-ft Aermotor; NHLR-registered 2023, county-administered, listed as standing; no access or staffing details found.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor steel truss tower with a square metal lookout cab, pyramidal roof and open metal staircase inside the truss

events.note: King William fire warden position created, per the 2014 county survey quoted by NHLR; the first fire tower followed shortly after
NHLR: 'This 80-foot Aermotor tower was built in 1935.' Builder not named
2014 historic survey by King William County, quoted in the NHLR description
Registered December 31, 2023; nominated by Krissy Reynolds; cooperator King William County Historic Preservation & Architectural Review Board

evidence.quote: This 80-foot Aermotor tower was built in 1935.

evidence.supports: fire warden post created 1933; first tower constructed shortly after
evidence.quote: The King William Fire Warden position was created in 1933 and the first fire tower was constructed shortly after.

evidence.supports: design: tall tapering metal truss with square lookout cab
evidence.quote: The fire tower is a tall tapering metal truss structure with a square plane metal frame lookout cab at the top.

evidence.supports: pyramidal roof; open metal staircase inside the truss
evidence.quote: The lookout cab has a pyramidal roof covered in seamed metal and is accessed by an open metal staircase located within the metal truss structure.
King William County Historic Preservation & Architectural Review Board

notes_for_editor: Two sources only, and the NHLR page carries nearly all the history. The 2014 county survey is quoted by NHLR, not read directly. Height converted from 80 ft to metres. Access, staffing and current condition are not documented, so no access key is given. The 2014 survey says the first tower went up 'shortly after' 1933, which fits the 1935 build date; no conflict found. The 1933 event is a warden post, not a tower, hence event type other. Two WebSearch-equivalent searches and four page reads were used.
